title: Fano negative fixed component of a polarized hyperkähler manifold with divisibility two
difficulty_reason: The authors identify the negative fixed component in a degenerating family with a plane sheaf-moduli space, combining the existing 2522 closed embedding with an explicit exclusion argument, equivariant linearization and a normalization/reduced-fibre argument; they then use Gorenstein and relative Picard properties to transport the canonical bundle and indivisibility to the smooth fibres. The author-supplied construction and 2522 proof are retained as proof material; the prior degeneration and fixed-component results explicitly cited to their earlier paper are attributed, not claimed newly proved here.

statement_spans.label: Original Theorem 1.3, including the canonical bundle formula

proof_spans.label: Author special-fibre construction and 2522 embedding proof
Author equivariant linearization, negative fibre identification, normality/reducedness and canonical bundle calculation

readability.basis: Existing 35-page reader from batch-14872-14875-r004; physically viewed page 3 with Theorem 1.3 and pages 23–24 with the final argument and continuation. Full author source retained, including the proof dependencies.

dedup.scope: Current master title searches for antisymplectic, fixed locus, hyper-kahler and hyperkähler; tex-body conjunction searches for antisymplectic with Fano or divisibility. Checked the two returned source entries and same-work author primary.

compared.relation: Same fixed work; selected Theorem 2.13 is a closed embedding of plane DUY moduli into a special K3 moduli space. It is a needed step for this theorem, whose conclusion concerns the Fano negative fixed component and its canonical bundle for divisibility-two polarizations.
Its selected primary is termination of a log-canonical MMP for Enriques pairs, not Fano geometry of negative fixed components of K3-type hyperkähler manifolds.

source_disclosures: The authors explicitly rely on their earlier paper involutions1 for the degeneration and the count of fixed components; these are cited dependencies, not supplied new proofs.
